meta.title: Tax rates: statutory and effective
meta.description: Nominal (statutory) rates from the law texts, effective rates of the very wealthy from research, and the parameters the interactive calculator needs. Research figures are static with an as_of date.

income_tax_top_rate.definition: Top marginal income tax rate ('Reichensteuer') on taxable income above 277 825 € (single), before the 5.5 % solidarity surcharge.

income_tax_top_threshold.definition: Taxable income (single) from which the 45 % rate applies in 2026.

income_tax_42_threshold.definition: Taxable income (single) from which the 42 % marginal rate applies in 2026.

solidarity_surcharge.source: § 4 SolzG 1995; exemption threshold § 3 SolzG (20 350 € income tax for singles in 2026)
solidarity_surcharge.definition: Solidarity surcharge as a percentage of the income or corporate tax. Since 2021 it is only levied on high incomes: for singles once the income tax exceeds 20 350 € (2026), with a sliding zone above that.

capital_income_flat_rate.definition: Flat withholding tax on private capital income (interest, dividends, realised gains on shares), plus 5.5 % solidarity surcharge on the tax = 26.375 % in total. Unrealised gains are not taxed.

corporate_income_tax.source: § 23 Abs. 1 KStG; reduction to 10 % in five steps from 2028 to 2032 enacted by the Gesetz für ein steuerliches Investitionssofortprogramm (Bundesrat, 11 July 2025)
corporate_income_tax.definition: Corporate income tax rate on retained and distributed profits of corporations (plus 5.5 % solidarity surcharge = 15.825 %). Falls by one point per year from 2028 to 10 % in 2032.

trade_tax_average.source: Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis), Pressemitteilung Nr. 309 vom 21. August 2025: durchschnittlicher Gewerbesteuer-Hebesatz 2024 409 %; Messzahl 3,5 % nach § 11 GewStG
trade_tax_average.definition: Effective municipal trade tax rate at the 2024 nationwide average multiplier: 3.5 % × 409 % ≈ 14.3 % of trade income. Together with corporate tax and surcharge, corporations pay about 30 % on profits.
trade_tax_average.refresh_hint: Destatis Realsteuervergleich / Gewerbesteuer press release each August.

inheritance_tax_class1_range.source: § 19 ErbStG (tax rates), § 16 ErbStG (personal allowances), §§ 13a, 13b ErbStG (business-asset relief)
inheritance_tax_class1_range.definition: Top rate of inheritance and gift tax for tax class I (spouse, children) — the scale runs from 7 % to 30 % depending on the taxable amount; class III (unrelated) 30–50 %. Children have a 400 000 € allowance per parent. Business assets can be 85 % or 100 % exempt under §§ 13a/13b ErbStG if the business is continued and payroll conditions are met.

wealth_tax.source: Bundesverfassungsgericht, Beschluss vom 22. Juni 1995 – 2 BvL 37/91; Vermögensteuer nicht mehr erhoben seit 1. Januar 1997 (Wikipedia: Vermögensteuer (Deutschland))
wealth_tax.definition: Germany's wealth tax has not been levied since 1997. The Constitutional Court found the unequal valuation of real estate versus other assets unconstitutional and set a deadline for reform (end of 1996) which the legislature let pass. The law formally still exists.

exit_tax.definition: Exit taxation: when a person who holds at least 1 % of a corporation moves abroad after at least 7 of the last 12 years of unlimited tax liability, the unrealised gain on those shares is treated as realised (fictitious sale) and taxed. The value 100 here means 'applies to 100 % of the fictitious gain'; the rate is the ordinary income tax rate under the partial-income method.

income_tax_top_rate.source: IRS, Revenue Procedure 2025-32 (tax year 2026 inflation adjustments); Tax Foundation summary
income_tax_top_rate.definition: Top federal marginal income tax rate, applying to taxable income above 640 600 USD (single) in 2026. State income taxes (0–13.3 %) come on top and are not included anywhere on this site.

capital_gains_top_rate.source: IRS Topic No. 409 (capital gains and losses); 2026 thresholds per Rev. Proc. 2025-32
capital_gains_top_rate.definition: Top federal rate on long-term capital gains and qualified dividends (taxable income above 545 500 USD, single, 2026), plus the 3.8 % net investment income tax = 23.8 %. Unrealised gains are not taxed; at death the cost basis is stepped up.

corporate_income_tax.source: IRS, Instructions for Form 1120 / 26 U.S.C. § 11 (flat 21 % since the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act 2017)
corporate_income_tax.definition: Federal corporate income tax rate. State corporate taxes (0–about 10 %) come on top.
corporate_income_tax.notes: source_url points to the IRS business-tax section; the statutory rate is 26 U.S.C. § 11(b).

estate_tax_top_rate.source: IRS, Estate Tax; basic exclusion amount 15 000 000 USD per person from 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32)
estate_tax_top_rate.definition: Top federal estate and gift tax rate on the value of an estate above the exclusion amount of 15 million USD per person (30 million per couple) in 2026.

wealth_tax.source: No federal wealth tax exists in the United States (proposals such as the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act were not enacted)
wealth_tax.definition: There is no annual tax on net wealth at the federal level. Local property taxes on real estate exist but are not a net-wealth tax.

rate.source: ProPublica, The Secret IRS Files (8 June 2021): the 25 richest Americans paid 13.6 bn USD in federal income taxes while their wealth grew by 401 bn USD — a 'true tax rate' of 3.4 %
rate.definition: Federal income tax paid divided by the growth in net worth (Forbes estimates, mostly unrealised gains) over 2014–2018. Not comparable with statutory rates, which apply to taxable income only.
rate.estimate_by: ProPublica, from leaked IRS data and Forbes wealth estimates

rate.source: White House Council of Economic Advisers and Office of Management and Budget, 23 September 2021: What Is the Average Federal Individual Income Tax Rate on the Wealthiest Americans?
rate.definition: Federal individual income taxes divided by income including unrealised capital gains, for the 400 wealthiest families, average 2010–2018.

effective.numerator: All federal, state and local taxes, including corporate taxes attributed to shareholders

rate.source: Emmanuel Saez & Gabriel Zucman, The Triumph of Injustice (2019) and presentation slides: 'Top 400 effective tax rate = 23 % (incl. corporate taxes, etc.) vs. 25–30 % for working & middle classes'; bottom 50 %: 24.2 % (reported by the New York Times, 6 October 2019)
rate.definition: All taxes (federal, state, local, including corporate taxes attributed to owners) as a share of pre-tax national income, 2018. Contested: the Tax Policy Center and others argue the authors overstate the rates of low-income households and understate those at the top; see the objections chapter.

rate.source: EU Tax Observatory, Global Tax Evasion Report 2024 (October 2023): global billionaires have effective personal tax rates equivalent to 0 % to 0.5 % of their wealth, largely because of the use of holding companies
rate.definition: Personal income taxes paid divided by net wealth. Upper end of the reported 0–0.5 % range (US billionaires about 0.5 %, French billionaires close to 0 %). A wealth-based rate cannot be compared with income-based rates.

rate.source: Gabriel Zucman, A blueprint for a coordinated minimum effective taxation standard for ultra-high-net-worth individuals (report commissioned by the Brazilian G20 presidency, June 2024)
rate.definition: Estimated effective personal tax rate of billionaires expressed as a share of their wealth (about 0.3 %). The report proposes a 2 % minimum tax on billionaire wealth.

effective.numerator: Corporate tax, trade tax, withholding tax on distributions and income tax, attributed to the owner

rate.source: Netzwerk Steuergerechtigkeit, Jahrbuch Steuergerechtigkeit 2026: the effective tax rate of billionaires fell from about 60 % (1996) to 29 % today; the enacted corporate tax cut lowers it by up to five further points by 2032
rate.definition: Model calculation for a typical German billionaire whose wealth sits in a corporation: all taxes on the company's profit plus taxes on the (small) distributed share, divided by the economic income including retained profits. The Jahrbuch 2024 puts real-estate billionaires at about 17 %.

effective.group: Owner of a holding company that retains all profits (statutory result, not a study)
effective.numerator: Personal income tax on distributions and realised gains

rate.source: § 32d EStG (Abgeltungsteuer applies only to distributed capital income and realised gains); § 8b KStG (dividends and gains between corporations 95 % exempt)
rate.definition: Personal tax due on profits that stay inside a holding company and on unrealised share-price gains: none. Only the corporate-level taxes (about 30 %) are paid until profits are distributed or shares are sold. This is what the law says, not an empirical measurement.

basic_allowance.definition: Grundfreibetrag 2026: taxable income up to this amount is tax-free (single).
basic_allowance.refresh_hint: § 32a EStG is amended for each year; copy the zone boundaries and polynomial coefficients.

zone2_upper.definition: Upper limit of the first progression zone: tax = (914.51 · y + 1 400) · y with y = (income − 12 348) / 10 000.

zone2_a.definition: Quadratic coefficient of the first progression zone.

zone2_b.definition: Linear coefficient of the first progression zone.

zone3_upper.definition: Upper limit of the second progression zone: tax = (173.10 · z + 2 397) · z + 1 034.87 with z = (income − 17 799) / 10 000.

zone3_a.definition: Quadratic coefficient of the second progression zone.

zone3_b.definition: Linear coefficient of the second progression zone.

zone3_c.definition: Constant of the second progression zone.

zone4_upper.definition: Upper limit of the 42 % zone: tax = 0.42 · x − 11 135.63.

zone5_c.definition: Constant subtracted in the 45 % zone: tax = 0.45 · x − 19 470.38.

soli_rate.definition: Solidarity surcharge rate on income tax.

soli_threshold.definition: Income tax amount (single) below which no solidarity surcharge is due; above it the surcharge is capped at 11.9 % of the difference (§ 4 Satz 2 SolzG).

soli_phase_in_rate.definition: Sliding-zone cap: the surcharge may not exceed 11.9 % of the difference between the income tax and the exemption threshold.

pension_rate_employee.source: Bundesregierung, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen 2026 (pension insurance contribution 18.6 %, half paid by the employee)
pension_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of the statutory pension contribution.

unemployment_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of the unemployment insurance contribution.

health_rate_employee.source: Bundesregierung, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen 2026: general contribution 14.6 % plus average supplementary contribution 2.9 %, each split equally
health_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of statutory health insurance: (14.6 % + 2.9 %) / 2.

care_rate_employee.source: Bundesregierung, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen 2026 (long-term care insurance 3.6 %, half employee; +0.6 points for childless members from age 23)
care_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of long-term care insurance for a member with children (childless: 2.4 %).

ceiling_pension_annual.source: Bundesregierung, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen 2026: 8 450 € per month in pension and unemployment insurance
ceiling_pension_annual.definition: Annual contribution ceiling for pension and unemployment insurance (12 × 8 450 €).

ceiling_health_annual.source: Bundesregierung, Beitragsbemessungsgrenzen 2026: 5 812.50 € per month in health and care insurance
ceiling_health_annual.definition: Annual contribution ceiling for health and long-term care insurance.

standard_deduction_single.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (tax year 2026); Tax Foundation summary
standard_deduction_single.definition: Standard deduction for single filers in 2026.
standard_deduction_single.refresh_hint: IRS inflation adjustments, published each October.

bracket1_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

bracket2_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

bracket3_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

bracket4_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

bracket5_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

bracket6_upper.source: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32; Tax Foundation 2026 brackets

social_security_rate_employee.source: IRS Topic No. 751 (Social Security and Medicare withholding rates)
social_security_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of the Social Security (OASDI) payroll tax, up to the wage base.

medicare_rate_employee.definition: Employee share of the Medicare payroll tax (no ceiling; +0.9 % above 200 000 USD not modelled).

social_security_wage_base.source: Social Security Administration, 2026 wage base announcement (24 October 2025), as reported by PayrollOrg
social_security_wage_base.definition: Maximum earnings subject to the Social Security payroll tax in 2026.
social_security_wage_base.refresh_hint: SSA COLA announcement each October: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html
